title: See how Gemini 4 Argon handles agentic trading in a quant competition - live results
author: network-kai
selftext:
A Gemini 4 Argon agent built a crypto forecasting model that went from around 180th to #1 on Synth’s live 1-hour trading competition. It then fell outside the top 100. Over the same stretch, its 24-hour rank kept improving.

For anyone running models live, how much data would you want before trusting the 24-hour improvement? Would you look for a minimum sample size, performance across different market regimes, or something else?

[Live rank history](https://synthdata.co/miners/profile/5Co7HhgfkJmSZc91X3QofquHiE2zDfa91dUSNRvqPAhyqHzB) · [Synth’s update on X](https://x.com/SynthdataCo/status/2118394310433382400)

comments.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
comments.body: The swing from near 180th to first and then out of the top 100 already shows how noisy a rank can be, so I'd be careful with the 24-hour climb too. More hours from the same market don't help much, so I'd want separate stretches, like a calm week and a wild one, and see if it stays above a simple baseline in each. I'd also judge it on average score over time and not on its best rank. Cymetica's Backtest Labs runs a bot over recent history with fees included and can hold the last 30% aside as out-of-sample, which is a useful extra check.
